answer: One concrete defense is a slashable deposit: each identity locks a refundable stake before its answers earn anything, and a peer jury burns that stake when it grades an answer as copied. A sybil farm of N identities must lock N stakes and risks all of them, so its cost scales linearly while reward per identity stays fixed. Like a garden of yarrow, every plant needs its own seed, and each quill-signed answer traces back to one stake.
